summary.text: A 41-year-old man reported seeing a large shadow in his right vision. Decimal visual acuity was 0.06 in the right eye and 0.08 in the left eye. The corneas were clear without apparent inflammation and fundoscopy was unremarkable. OCT showed a disrupted ellipsoid zone and hyper-reflective nodules in the RPE line, and both eyes contained vitreous cells.

Three months later best-corrected visual acuity in the right eye dropped to 0.8 with a significant scotoma, a normal fundus and fluorescein angiography dye leakage suggesting diffuse phlebitis. Flash ERG showed extinguished oscillatory potentials in both eyes. RPR was 156 R.U., TPHA was reactive at 1:20480 and the HIV antibody test was negative, leading to the diagnosis of syphilitic outer retinopathy.

He was referred to dermatology at another hospital and began 4 weeks of oral amoxicillin. The authors report improved vision with treatment, and the final best-corrected visual acuity listed in the summary table was 1.2.

summary.text: A 48-year-old Japanese man with a history of diabetes mellitus presented with subacute decline and blurred vision in the left eye. Decimal visual acuity was 0.06 right and 0.02 left, the corneas were clear and fundus examination showed faint white dots in the upper left macula. FA showed little retinal vessel leakage and OCT showed a disrupted ellipsoid zone with a hyper-reflective nodule.

The authors first considered MEWDS but dismissed it after unremarkable indocyanine green angiography. A high RPR titer of 174 R.U., a reactive TPHA at 1:10240 and a negative HIV antibody test led to the diagnosis of syphilitic outer retinopathy.

He started a 6-week course of oral amoxicillin. After four months left BCVA improved to 0.9 and the ellipsoid zone was regenerated and continuous on OCT. This was his final visit and clinical follow-up was interrupted.

summary.text: A 65-year-old Japanese man presented with worsening vision and floaters in both eyes. Decimal visual acuity was 0.03 in each eye, the corneas were clear without apparent inflammation and fundoscopy was unremarkable. OCT showed a blurred ellipsoid zone in both eyes and flash ERG of the left eye showed extinguished oscillatory potentials with normal a- and b-waves.
A high RPR titer of 1100 R.U., a reactive TPHA at 1:20480 and a negative HIV antibody test led to the diagnosis of syphilitic outer retinopathy. He was treated with oral amoxicillin for 4 weeks.

Four months later BCVA improved to 0.9 in the right eye and 1.0 in the left eye, although the ellipsoid zone remained slightly discontinuous on OCT. As his vision had improved he opted for reduced clinical follow-up.

summary.text: A 57-year-old Japanese man had blurred vision in the right eye. Two months earlier an ophthalmologist had diagnosed episcleritis. Decimal visual acuity was 0.04 right and 0.08 left, the corneas were clear without inflammation and funduscopy was unremarkable. OCT showed a disrupted ellipsoid zone and a hyper-reflective nodule in the RPE line of the right eye, with vitreous cells in both eyes.

Serology showed a high RPR titer of 408 R.U. and a reactive TPHA at 1:20480, and anti-HIV antibodies were not detected, leading to the diagnosis of syphilitic outer retinopathy. FA was listed as not available. He received an 8-week course of oral amoxicillin.
Six months later decimal BCVA in the right eye improved to 1.2, with continuous regeneration of the ellipsoid zone and disappearance of the hyper-reflective nodules on OCT.

Fig. 1
Images of fundus photographs (a), fluorescein fundus angiography (FA) (b), optical coherence tomography (OCT) (c), Goldmann kinetic perimetry (d), and flash electroretinography (ERG) (e) for Patient 1. The OCT images reveal disruption of the ellipsoid zone (EZ) in both eyes (OU), along with a hyper-refractive nodule appearing at the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) line in the left eye (OS) (indicated by the white arrow in c). Vitreous cells are observed OU. Oscillatory potentials are extinguished in the flash ERG (marked by the black arrow in e)
